extracted.intended_audience: graduate or advanced undergraduate students studying module theory and category theory (and instructors preparing courses/notes)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, lemmas, and theorems about exact sequences of modules (short exact sequences, splitting, Snake/Five/Nine Lemmas, projective modules, finite generation/presentation) and category-theoretic constructions (categories, functors, adjoints, direct limits, coproducts, coequalizers) intended to teach and formalize these concepts and their interrelations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness at a term / exact sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence of module homomorphisms ... -> A -> B -> C -> ... is exact at B if Im(previous map) = Ker(next map). The sequence is exact if it is exact at every term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used throughout: e.g., exactness of 0 -> L -> M -> N -> 0 is characterized by injectivity/surjectivity and kernel/cokernel relations; many proofs reduce to checking kernel and image equalities (see (5.1)-(5.3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Short exact sequence (definition and characterization)
rubrics_metrics.description: A short exact sequence 0 -> L -> M -> N -> 0 is called short exact; it is exact iff the first map is injective, the second map is surjective, L = Ker(second map), and N = Coker(first map).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often identify L as a submodule of M and N as the quotient M/L. Example sequences are given; exercises show how short exact sequences behave under standard constructions (extensions, direct sums).

rubrics_metrics.name: Splitting of short exact sequences (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A short exact sequence 0 -> M' -> M -> M'' -> 0 splits if there is an isomorphism φ: M ≅ M' ⊕ M'' with φ restricting to the inclusion/projection on M' and M'' respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Splitting is equivalent to existence of a retraction M -> M' or a section M'' -> M (Proposition 5.9). Exercises point out common misstatements and consequences of splitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retract and section (for split sequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: A retraction r: M -> M' of an injection i: M' -> M satisfies r∘i = 1_{M'}. A section s: M'' -> M of a surjection p: M -> M'' satisfies p∘s = 1_{M''}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existence of either yields splitting; proofs show how to construct the complementary map and verify identities, using UMP arguments and exactness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness preserved by direct sums/products (Proposition 5.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a family of sequences indexed by I, if every sequence is exact then so are the induced sequences formed by direct sums (⊕_I) and products (∏_I); conversely, exactness of either induced sequence implies exactness of each original one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate from componentwise definitions of kernel and cokernel; used to transport exactness across coproducts/products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induced exact sequence on submodules (Lemma 5.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given 0 -> M' -> M -> M'' -> 0 and a submodule N ⊆ M, set N' := preimage of N in M' and N'' := image of N in M''. Then 0 -> N' -> N -> N'' -> 0 is short exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: check exactness directly; used in exercises and constructions involving subobjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Snake Lemma (Lemma 5.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a commutative diagram with exact rows, there is a long exact sequence relating kernels and cokernels (the usual connecting morphism @): Ker(f') -> Ker(f) -> Ker(f'') -> Coker(f') -> Coker(f) -> Coker(f'').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes construction of the connecting morphism by diagram chase, verification that it's well-defined, and checking exactness at each term. Also: if certain maps are injective/surjective then induced maps inherit these properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five Lemma (Exercise 5.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a commutative diagram with exact rows, (1) if maps at positions 3 and 1 are surjective and position 0 is injective then middle map is surjective; (2) if positions 3 and 1 are injective and position 4 is surjective then middle map is injective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by diagram chase; standard lemma for deducing isomorphisms from surrounding isomorphisms under exactness hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nine Lemma (Exercise 5.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a 3×3 commutative diagram with exact columns and middle row exact, the first (top) row is exact iff the third (bottom) row is exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Snake Lemma to a suitable subdiagram; used to relate exactness across rows in a grid of short exact sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifting in diagrams (Exercise 5.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a commutative diagram with exact rows where certain vertical maps are surjective, one can lift compatible elements: if some maps are surjective, for given n in N and m'' in M'' with compatibility, there exists m in M with prescribed images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard lifting/patching lemma used in constructions and proofs involving surjective maps and compatibility conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Left exactness of Hom (Theorem 5.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a sequence M' -> M -> M'' -> 0, the sequence is exact iff for all modules N the induced sequence 0 -> Hom(M'' , N) -> Hom(M, N) -> Hom(M', N) is exact. Dually, 0 -> N' -> N -> N'' exact iff for all M, 0 -> Hom(M, N') -> Hom(M, N) -> Hom(M, N'') is exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterizes cokernel/universal mapping property via Hom and shows Hom(–, N) is left-exact; proof reduces to UMP of cokernel and kernel arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentations and finite presentation (Definition 5.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: A (free) presentation of M is an exact sequence G -> F -> M -> 0 with G and F free. If G and F are finite rank, the presentation is finite and M is finitely presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 5.19 constructs presentations from generators; exercises explore relationships between finite generation of kernels and finite presentation of quotient modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective module (Definition 5.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: A module P is projective if for every surjection π : M -> N and every map f: P -> N there exists a lift g: P -> M with π∘g = f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Free modules are projective (Exercise 5.21). Projectivity characterized by several equivalent conditions in Theorem 5.22 (splitting short exact sequences, summand of free module, Hom functor exactness, lifting property).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent characterizations of projective modules (Theorem 5.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: For module P, equivalent statements: (1) P is projective; (2) every short exact 0 -> K -> M -> P -> 0 splits; (3) P is a direct summand of a free module (exists K with K ⊕ P ≅ free); (4) Hom(P, –) is exact on exact sequences; (5) Hom(P, π) is surjective for every surjection π.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof shows implications around lifting, splitting, and Hom exactness. Useful criteria for recognizing projectivity in practice and for constructing splittings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schanuel's Lemma (Lemma 5.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two short exact sequences 0 -> L -> P -> M -> 0 and 0 -> L' -> P' -> M -> 0 with P and P' projective, there is an isomorphism relating these sequences yielding K ≅ L ⊕ P' ≅ P ⊕ L'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructs intermediate maps using projectivity and shows the resulting direct-sum relations; used to compare projective presentations of the same module.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite generation/presentation under short exact sequences (Propositions 5.26–5.28 and Exercises)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propositions/exercises assert: if 0 -> L -> M -> N -> 0 with L finitely generated and M finitely presented then N is finitely presented (5.26); dually if M and N finitely generated/presented then other terms inherit finite generation/presentation under conditions (5.27, 5.28); exercise 5.24 relates finite presentation of M and finite generation of L when 0 -> L -> R^n -> M -> 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs use presentations, the Snake Lemma, and standard exact-sequence arguments to pass finiteness properties along short exact sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories (definition and examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: A category C consists of objects and sets Hom_C(A,B) of morphisms with associative composition and identity maps; examples: Sets, Rings, R-mod (R-modules), R-alg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic categorical language used throughout later sections on functors, natural transformations, adjoints, and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functors and natural transformations (definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A (covariant) functor F: C -> C' assigns objects and maps preserving composition and identities. A natural transformation η: F -> F' is a family of maps η(A): F(A) -> F'(A) commuting with action of morphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Hom_R(M, –) as a functor, forgetful functor from R-mod to Sets. Naturality diagrams are emphasized and used in adjointness proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjoint functors (definition and unit/counit characterization)
rubrics_metrics.description: An adjoint pair (F ⊣ F') satisfies natural bijections Hom_{C'}(F(A), A') ≅ Hom_C(A, F'(A')) for all A, A'. The unit η: 1_C -> F'F and counit ε: FF' -> 1_{C'} satisfy universal properties and determine the adjunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructions show adjoints are unique up to canonical isomorphism; examples: free module functor left adjoint to forgetful functor, polynomial ring functor left adjoint to forgetful functor from R-alg to Sets. Exercise 6.5 treats unit universality and converses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct limit / colimit (definition and universal property) (6.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a small index category I and a functor i ↦ M_i, the direct limit lim_{→} M_i is an object P with insertion maps M_i -> P compatible with transition maps, universal among such objects; equivalently the left adjoint of the diagonal functor Δ: C -> C^I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notation lim_{→} M_i or lim_{→, i∈I} M_i. Universality determines the limit up to unique isomorphism; explicit constructions given in many concrete categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coproducts as special case of direct limits (6.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The coproduct ⨿_{i∈I} M_i is the universal object with inclusion maps from each M_i; when I discrete, coproduct = direct limit. In R-mod, coproduct is direct sum ⊕; in Sets it's disjoint union ⊔.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial object corresponds to empty coproduct. Insertions/inclusions satisfy universal mapping property used to define maps out of coproducts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coequalizers as special case of direct limits (6.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two parallel maps f,g: M -> N, their coequalizer is the universal object P with map q: N -> P such that q∘f = q∘g; in R-mod it's Coker(f-g) and in Sets it's quotient by the smallest equivalence relation identifying f(m) with g(m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coequalizers obtained as direct limits over a small 2-object category; coequalizer of f and 0 is Coker(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of direct limits ⇔ existence of coproducts and coequalizers (Lemma 6.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: A category C has all direct limits iff it has coproducts and coequalizers; similarly a functor preserves all direct limits iff it preserves coproducts and coequalizers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct direct limits by forming a coproduct of all objects and then coequalizing maps induced by transitions; practical criterion to check existence/preservation of colimits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct limits exist in R-mod and Sets (Theorem 6.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: The categories R-mod and Sets have direct limits (since they have coproducts and coequalizers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to justify concrete constructions of colimits in these common categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Left adjoints preserve direct limits (Theorem 6.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every left adjoint functor F: C -> C' preserves direct limits: F(lim_{→} M_i) ≅ lim_{→} F(M_i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses adjunction and the universal mapping property; corollary: left adjoints commute with colimits like coproducts/coequalizers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functor categories inherit direct limits (Proposition 6.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: If C has direct limits indexed by a small category K, then the functor category C^J (functors J -> C) also has direct limits indexed by K, computed pointwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: take limits at each object of J; naturality and uniqueness follow from componentwise universality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct limits commute (Theorem 6.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a bifunctor-indexed system, iterated direct limits commute: lim_{→,α∈A} lim_{→,β∈B} M_{α,β} ≅ lim_{→,β∈B} lim_{→,α∈A} M_{α,β}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows because lim_{→,β} is a left adjoint and functor categories have direct limits; used to interchange colimits in proofs and constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: lim_{→} preserves coproducts and coequalizers in common categories (Corollary 6.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a small index category I and C = Sets or R-mod, the direct limit functor lim_{→}: C^I -> C preserves coproducts and coequalizers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate from previous theorems since coproducts and coequalizers are colimits and lim_{→} is a left adjoint in functor categories.
